title: Packed int12 exporter/runtime mismatch causing crash loops and silent accuracy drift
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary: On 2025-10-29 we observed a production incident where a subset of models exported with the new vendor exporter (exporter-v2) in packed int12 weight format caused runtime worker crash loops under concurrent load and a correlated silent accuracy drift for a small but high-value RLHF customer cohort. This ticket tracks post-incident remediation, long-term prevention, and rollout controls.

Impact: intermittent crash loops on Dedicated nodes serving packed-int12 variants; fallback to fp16/int8 occurred for some traffic but not consistently, resulting in a period (~90 minutes) of elevated latency and measurable BLEU/QA score degradation for a small set of queries. No data exfiltration reported.

Scope: affected serving runtime path that handles packed weight parsing, operator registration for the new fused attention kernel, and exporter/loader compatibility checks. Also uncovered gaps in canary traffic ramping and telemetry for operator-level fallback events.
timeline:
2025-10-29 02:07 UTC: First crash alert from Dedicated pool (high error-rate).
2025-10-29 02:12 UTC: Pager escalation and initial rollback to previous serving config for affected service.
2025-10-29 02:35 UTC: Partial recovery after rolling back exporter-v2 bundles; some nodes still experienced rare crashes.
2025-10-29 03:40 UTC: Identified unpacking mismatch in runtime that misinterpreted packed int12 block headers (endianness + stride mismatch).
2025-10-29 05:10 UTC: Canary test run reproduces crash locally with exporter-v2 artifact and high-concurrency test harness.
2025-10-29 07:00 UTC: Temporary mitigation: strict model acceptance gate added and exporter-v2 artifacts quarantined.
2025-10-30 to 2025-11-02: Root cause analysis, additional telemetry added to canary harness.
2025-11-03: Ticket opened to track corrective work and long-term prevention.
root_cause: A mismatch between exporter-v2 packed int12 layout and the runtime's unpacker: the exporter changed the header/stride encoding for 12-bit packed blocks to improve disk size and I/O, but the runtime kernel assumed the prior header format. Under high-concurrency this led to malformed memory accesses and heap corruption that surfaced as crash loops. Additionally, for some model variants the fallback policy did not trigger immediately due to missing operator-fingerprint telemetry, causing silent accuracy degradation until manual rollback. The exporter change was not gated by a runtime compatibility test in CI or by a gating matrix in model onboarding docs.
mitigations:
Immediate: quarantine exporter-v2 bundles and rollback to exporter-v1 for all affected model artifacts; emergency canary hold and disable automatic promotion for packed formats.
Short-term: ship runtime hotfix to add defensive validation when parsing packed blocks (header checksum + bounds checks) and enable immediate operator fingerprint emission on parse error.
Long-term: add exporter/runtime compatibility matrix, formalize packed-format versioning with a schema header and backward-compatibility flags, and require end-to-end canary with concurrency stress for any new packed weight format.
